# Text that doesn't belong in this public repository. scripts/check-public-text.sh
# reads it. One rule per line: NAME:FLAGS:REGEX
#   NAME   the rule's id in the report
#   FLAGS  "i" for case-insensitive, "-" for case-sensitive
#   REGEX  a Python regular expression, matched against each line
# An exception goes in allowlist.txt, never here. Lines starting with # are comments.
# Names this file shouldn't spell out, such as people, deals, hosts and
# private repositories, are in hashed.txt instead.

# Ticket keys and finding ids. allowlist.txt drops SHA-256, UTF-8, RFC-n and the like.
ticket:-:\b[A-Z]{2,}-[0-9]+\b
# Secret names that carry a ticket number
ticket-secret:-:\bIT_[0-9]{4,}\w*
# Jira and Confluence links
jira:i:mirantis\.jira\.com|atlassian\.net
# Google Docs and Drive
gdocs:i:docs\.google\.com|drive\.google\.com
# Meeting notes
granola:i:granola\.ai
# Slack links and channels
slack:i:[a-z0-9-]*\.?slack\.com
# RFC 1918 addresses. allowlist.txt keeps the generic ones in examples and tests.
private-ip:-:\b(10\.[0-9]{1,3}|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])|192\.168)\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\b
# Home and runner paths
home-path:-:/Users/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+|/private/tmp/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+|/home/[a-z][a-z0-9_-]+/
# Email addresses. allowlist.txt keeps noreply and the reserved example domains.
email:-:[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}
# GitHub logins
gh-login:i:\b(retrospct|jeremypruitt)\b
# Commercial wording. The bracket keeps this file from holding the word itself.
commercial:i:\bc[u]stomers?\b
partner:i:\bpartners?\b
# Internal requirement documents
prd:-:\bPRD\b|\bMVP[- ]?[0-9]*\b
# Environment names
staging:i:\bstaging\b
# AI attribution
ai-trailer:i:co-authored-by|generated with
ai-tool:-:\bClaude\b|claude\.ai|\bCursor\b|cursoragent|anthropic\.com
# AWS account ids: 12 digits within 40 characters after aws or account
aws-account:i:(aws|account)[^0-9]{0,40}\b[0-9]{12}\b
# Internal requirement ids, such as R12 and perf.6
requirement-id:-:\bR[0-9]{2,3}\b|\bperf\.[0-9]+\b
# A measurement dated or tied to a build. Say what the user sees instead
measured-on:i:\bmeasured (on|at) (20[0-9]{2}-|dev\.[0-9])
# A measured run time, such as "1 hour 50 minutes" or "1h 54m"
measured-time:i:\b[0-9]+ ?(h|hours?) [0-9]+ ?(m|min|minutes)\b
# A machine type from a test run. The API's own enum keeps it in the client
machine-type:-:\bGB300\b
